# Claude Code for PMs — full content dump

Open-source templates, skills, and best practices for product managers using
Claude Code. Repo: https://github.com/runtm-ai/claudecode-for-pms (MIT).

## 10 best practices (one-line each)

1. Write the PRD before the prompt — answers problem, user, done, out-of-scope.
2. Use plan mode for anything non-trivial — negotiate the plan, not the diff.
3. Make CLAUDE.md the single source of truth — product / voice / stack / conventions.
4. Author skills, not prompts — they auto-load by trigger phrase.
5. Ship a DESIGN.md with brand tokens — at the source so contributors can't reach default indigo.
6. Wire up the right MCPs early — GitHub, Linear, Notion, PostHog. Real data, not a paraphrase.
7. Never commit a secret — .env in .gitignore, MCP tokens from the shell.
8. Treat the design system as a skill — colors / type / voice / surfaces, all in one SKILL.md.
9. Generate ad assets with Remotion — programmatic video, deterministic output.
10. Onboard the agent like a teammate — first-day reading list, code map, voice doc.

## Six shipped skills (skills/<name>/SKILL.md)

- writing-prds              — PRD authoring with 9-section output and clarifying questions
- writing-release-notes     — Merged PRs to customer-facing notes by audience
- writing-stakeholder-updates — Per-audience weekly updates (eng leads, exec, CS, cross-team)
- synthesizing-user-research — Transcripts to themes, JTBD, next step
- prioritizing-features     — Framework picker (RICE, MoSCoW, WSJF, Kano) + scored backlog
- your-brand                — Fill-in template for color, type, voice, surfaces

## Templates in the repo

- CLAUDE.md                 — what Claude reads on session start
- DESIGN.md                 — brand tokens, voice, surface rules
- pr_flow/create-prd.mdc    — explicit PRD-authoring rule
- pr_flow/generate-tasks.mdc — PRD to task list
- pr_flow/process-task-list.mdc — work the list sub-task at a time
- mcp.json.example          — MCP servers for GitHub / Linear / Notion / PostHog
- .env.example              — env keys, never values

## Voice we wrote in

Plainspoken, period-end declarative. No buzzwords (unlock, leverage, seamless,
robust, next-generation). Specific nouns over abstractions. Numbers when we
have them.
